review_reference: UNSIGNED: reviewed_by stays empty until the owner signs. Release A integration (coordinator's hand-over of 18 November 2026 on hid-system#258; Rahman integration owner, DB). One owner signature for 0128-0137: 0128 (#264), 0129 (#266), 0130 and 0131 (#272), 0132 (#273), 0133 and 0134 (#280, Ola), 0135 (#274), 0136 (#275), 0137 (#276). Owner decisions followed: Q100 B, Q101, Q102, Q103 A, Q104, Q105, Q106, Q108 A, Q109 (also: no daily limit on registration without a NIN, coordinator 19 November), Q110, Q111 A, Q112 A, Q113 A, and ORD-2. Q114-Q120 are open; Q119 and Q120 touch 0133 and are built as recommended unless the owner says otherwise. Releases after 0124-0127 (live); production's pending set is then exactly the files below.
evidence: Each file's suite, the full database suites and the PG16 upgrade rehearsal on throwaway clusters with fictional data only, as posted on hid-system#258 with the sha256 of each file. 0128: the PIN-use inbox notice naming the clinician, role and facility; the access-request list names the requester. 0129: a staff member's chosen facility kept per sign-in (behind STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE, off by default). 0130: front-desk registration without a NIN (phone required except for a child; the desk creates the record with no possible duplicate, otherwise an approver who did not start it decides); no daily limit (Q109), the facility's count today only for an operations alert. 0131: doctors, nurses and clinicians open their own facility's patient for 24 hours without a PIN (registered here or a consented visit here in 24 months), shown in the patient's access history and revocable by the patient. 0132: staff patient search (strong keys everywhere, weak keys own facility only) and emergency search by exact names and date of birth (break-glass holders, a reason, shown in the patient's access log); cards carry a 10-minute matchRef, never a Health ID or patient id. 0133 (ORD-2): this facility's pharmacist and lab scientist work on its own prescriptions and lab requests without a consent grant (the work items and their chain only, never the chart; a patient's deny directive still applies), and an activated prescription goes automatically to the hospital's own pharmacy when it is staffed; a hold or an edit withdraws the send and the prescriber is told. 0134 (Q102): a fictional pharmacist and lab scientist at the sealed QA tenant's QA Hospital, sealed QA only. 0135: the waiting list (check-in by matchRef or own-facility patient, stage, triage, assignee; no clinical content; not a visit). 0136: the role-table changes of Q103 A with Q111 A and Q112 A; stops at apply, changing nothing, if any real (non-sealed) staff would be affected (Q113 A). 0137: QoreID asked once per NIN, its stored answer and its hold; a record not yet on a Health ID kept 90 days (Q110), a NIN-only record a sign-up cannot use answered from storage, QoreID's not found for every check, and a matched record's keep (never shortened). LOCKS: every file that changes or references an existing table takes those tables first, NOWAIT, at the strongest mode it takes (measured with pg_locks before commit): retried every 100 ms for at most 5 seconds, else 55P03 with nothing applied; inside the runner's dry run, where the transaction already holds the earlier files' locks, one attempt and no sleep (0133 as Ola wrote it; 0130, 0131, 0132, 0135 and 0136 since 19 November). 0128 is the first file, so it holds nothing when it starts; 0129 retries for at most 5 seconds without the one-attempt rule, so in the dry run it can keep 0128's lock on identity.outbox_events for up to 5 seconds while it waits (to be added with 0129's re-hash). FILE BY FILE: the runner applies each pending file in its own transaction; the rehearsal proves today's live images (staging a9196203) pass their runtime verifiers on the schema left after 0132, after 0135 and after 0137. Every file is additive or replaces bodies it pins by md5; runtime-grants.sql grants exactly what the files grant.
